title: Li-Kaleyski Conjecture 11 root-freeness criterion
summary: Prove the exact root-freeness criterion conjectured for the second bivariate polynomial underlying the Li-Kaleyski trivariate APN family.

formal_statement.body: Let $i>1$ and $m$ be positive integers with $\gcd(i,m)=1$ and put $q=2^i$. Define $P_{11}(X,Y)=X^{q^2+q+1}+X^{q+1}Y^{q^2}+XY^q+X^qY^{q^2}+X^{q^2}Y+X^{q^2}+Y^{q^2+q+1}+Y^{q^2+1}+Y^{q^2+q}+Y^{q^2}+1$. Prove that $P_{11}$ has no zero in $\mathbb F_{2^m}^2$ if and only if $\gcd(m,7)=1$, or give a counterexample to either implication.

scope.domain: Root-freeness of the Conjecture 11 polynomial controlling a trivariate APN construction
assumptions: Roots are sought in the Cartesian square $\mathbb F_{2^m}^2$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves the $i=1$ specialization in Proposition 12. The equivalence for every coprime pair with $i>1$ remains unproved, and the broader triprojective reformulation in later work does not prove this exact binary criterion.

citations.label: Li--Kaleyski, Two New Infinite Families of APN Functions in Trivariate Form

progress.summary: The source conjectures a second if-and-only-if root-freeness criterion and proves only its i=1 specialization.
